destination.name: Gundagai
destination.tagline: A Hume Highway town behind the Dog on the Tuckerbox and a marble cathedral model.
destination.description: Gundagai is a Hume Highway town on the Murrumbidgee River, a byword for outback Australia in songs and poems such as Along the Road to Gundagai. Eight kilometres north, the Dog on the Tuckerbox monument, unveiled in 1932, is a tribute to bullockies based on an 1850s poem. In town, Rusconi's Marble Masterpiece is a miniature cathedral hand-built from more than 20,000 pieces of marble. The town moved up the slopes of Mount Parnassus after the 1852 flood killed 83 of its 250 residents.
whyVisit: See the Dog on the Tuckerbox

goodToKnow.title: Dog on the Tuckerbox
goodToKnow.detail: The monument is 8 km north of town just off the Hume Highway, with a kiosk and farm shop open daily, and is open 24 hours.

goodToKnow.title: Marble cathedral hours
goodToKnow.detail: Rusconi's Marble Masterpiece is open Mon–Fri 9 am–4:30 pm (closed 12:30–1 pm) and Sat–Sun 10 am–3 pm; entry about $5.

goodToKnow.title: No public transport
goodToKnow.detail: There is no public transport in Gundagai, and South Gundagai is about an hour on foot from the main shopping strip in the north.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} avoid the hot, dry summers and the cool, cloudy winters of the South West Slopes.
